summary: Phase 10 Notifications (frontend only) verified. Newly-registered buyer sees NotificationBell in top nav (empty state, no badge). After buyer sends a message from a listing and seller replies, buyer receives a live {type:'notification', notif_type:'NewMessage', title:'New message'} frame over wss://.../api/ws/messages, the notification-badge appears with count 1 WITHOUT reload, and the dropdown shows the notification-item titled 'New message'. Mark-all-read hides the badge; a subsequent seller reply re-increments the badge; clicking a notification-item marks it read and navigates. All 5 nav links render for a logged-in user and no blocking console errors.

integration_issues.issue: Each 'notification' frame is observed twice per event on the buyer page (two WS connections to /api/ws/messages are briefly concurrent across route transitions). Badge still increments correctly by exactly 1 per event (setCount is invoked from the currently-mounted component only), so no user-visible bug, but there is a small window where two /api/ws/messages sockets are open in parallel. Consider ensuring the previous socket is fully closed before opening a new one on route change or gating on ws.readyState.

action_items: Optional: dedupe /api/ws/messages connections in NotificationBell/messages page to avoid transient double-open on route change (no functional impact today).
critical_code_review_comments: NotificationBell opens a dedicated WS to /api/ws/messages in addition to the one opened by the Messages page; consider centralising the WS in a context/provider so a single connection serves both consumers.
The dropdown renders items only if user is logged in; there is no error state if /api/notifications fails (silently caught). Consider surfacing an error/retry in the dropdown.
ROUTE_FOR fallback goes to /dashboard for unknown notif_types — acceptable but should be documented.
